Requirements: The application for the Master of Architecture program requires an online application, a Statement of Purpose with a maximum of 750 words, an additional short response of up to 500 words, three letters of recommendation, transcripts from previous institutions, and a nonrefundable $70 application fee. Additionally, Graduate Record Exam (GRE) general test results are required. A portfolio of creative work is also a key component of the application.
Department: College of Architecture, Design, and the Arts
Description: The Master of Architecture is a professional degree program for students holding a pre-professional undergraduate degree in architecture or a bachelor’s degree in another field. The curriculum is designed to educate students in the history and theory of architecture, environmental and technical systems, digital fabrication, and professional practice. The core of the program is the design studio, a laboratory for research and synthesis in which the broad concerns of the discipline and profession are tested and applied. The program culminates in a design thesis that demonstrates the student’s ability to use architectural design as a form of critical inquiry.
Accredidation: The Master of Architecture is accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB).

Requirements: Applicants must have earned at least a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college in the United States or a comparable degree from a recognized institution of higher learning abroad. A grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (A=4.0), or comparable GPA for an international applicant, for the last two years of undergraduate study is a minimum requirement for admission. Please note that proposed programs of study may require a higher GPA than the Graduate College's minimum standard. [1]
Description: The Master of Arts program in art history is designed to provide the student with a broad knowledge of the major art historical periods, the scholarly and bibliographical resources, and the methodologies of art history. It also offers an opportunity to investigate art historical problems in some depth. [1]

Requirements: Applicants are considered on an individual basis. In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: Baccalaureate Field Applicants must have either an undergraduate major in history or a minimum of 16 semester hours in history. Grade Point Average At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study. A GPA of 3.50/4.00 is recommended. [3]
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description: The UIC Master of Arts in the Teaching of History (MAT) is a program for students who wish to combine advanced historical training with preparation for a teaching career. The program can be taken with or without teacher licensure. The licensure track of the MAT program leads to a Professional Educator License (PEL) in the state of Illinois, with an endorsement to teach social studies in grades 9-12. The program includes courses in historical content, teaching methods, and a student teaching experience. The non-licensure track is designed for current teachers or those who do not need a teaching license.
Accredidation: The teacher education programs at the University of Illinois Chicago are accredited by the Illinois State Board of Education (ISBE).

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Art History
Requirements:
In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements:

*   Baccalaureate Field: No restrictions.
*   Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study.
*   Letters of Recommendation: Three required from faculty members or others familiar with the applicant's training, ability, and experience. [13]
*   Personal Statement: Applicants must submit a short statement of purpose (1–2 pages). [13]
*   Writing Sample: Applicants must submit a sample of their written work (approximately 15 pages). [13]
*   Curriculum Vitae: Applicants must submit a list of their academic and professional achievements (1-3 pages). [13]
*   English Proficiency Requirement for International Applicants: Please refer to the UIC Admissions website for details.
Department: College of Architecture, Design, and the Arts
Concentration: ['History of Architecture and Art', 'Black Studies', 'Central and Eastern European Studies', "Gender and Women's Studies", 'Museum and Exhibition Studies', 'Violence Studies']
Description: The Master of Arts in Art History offers emphases in the history of architecture and art. This intensive four-semester program offers students an opportunity to explore advanced seminars in art history. [4] MA students may take coursework in ancient, medieval, early modern, and modern art, with a geographic focus in South Asia, Anatolia, Europe and the Americas. [4] Whether you write qualifying papers or a thesis, this program of study is intended for students with a BA in any field who want to pursue work in museums, galleries, education, government advocacy, social justice or any of the other myriad careers where advanced knowledge of the visual and built environment is useful. [4]
Accredidation: The University of Illinois Chicago is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). [15] Information regarding specific accreditation for the Master of Arts in Art History program is not mentioned on the university's website.

Requirements: Applicants are considered on an individual basis. In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: Baccalaureate Field: No restrictions. Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study. Tests Required: GRE not required. Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation addressing the applicant's academic accomplishments and potential. Personal Statement: Required. A personal statement of academic and professional intent and research interests. [9]
Concentration: ['Black Studies (Interdepartmental Graduate Concentration)', "Gender and Women's Studies (Interdepartmental Concentration)", 'Latin American and Latino Studies (Interdepartmental Concentration)', 'Museum and Exhibition Studies', 'Violence Studies (Interdepartmental Graduate Concentration)']
Description: Our faculty ahere to core research interests on a wide range of topics and are specifically focussed on issues related to urbanism, environment and landscapes, health and mobilities in the present and past. The Graduate program provides opportunities for students to expand their interests through Terminal MA and PhD degrees in the three major subfields of Archaeology, Biological Anthropology, and Sociocultural Anthropology. The competitive admissions process is committed to selecting a diverse range of students whose backgrounds and interests will complement the broader research interests of the department. Our two-year, coursework-based MA is designed to provide students with opportunities to pursue career tracks within and beyond Anthropology: Academic – Students will gain a broader knowledge base and research skills in the discipline with the goal of pursuing further graduate education. Cultural Heritage – Students will learn and practice skills in Museum Anthropology or Cultural Resource Management. Bioarchaeology – Students willl gain skills in the assessment of human remains, the diagnosis of ancient diseases, and the identification of faunal remains. Students with interests in NAGPRA are especially encouraged to apply.

Requirements:
Applicants are considered on an individual basis. Complete transcripts of all undergraduate and any graduate work must be submitted. Besides the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements:

*   Baccalaureate Field: No restrictions. Applicants must have the equivalent of 20 semester hours of study in communication or related programs of social inquiry, such as political science and sociology.
*   Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study.
*   Letters of Recommendation: Three required, each along with a completed Rating Form, at least two from academic recommenders. [3, 6]
*   Other Requirements: Students are only admitted for the fall semester. [3, 6]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Criminology, Law, and Justice
Requirements:
In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must also meet the following program requirements:

*   Baccalaureate Field: Applicants must have a baccalaureate degree in criminology, law, and justice or a related field from an accredited college or university.
*   Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study. [2]
*   Letters of Recommendation: Three are required, preferably from professors familiar with the student's recent work or from supervisors for applicants with professional experience. [2]
*   English Proficiency: International students must meet minimum English proficiency test scores (TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE Academic). [2]
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description: The Department of Criminology, Law, and Justice at UIC is an interdisciplinary Masters, Ph.D. and undergraduate program at Chicago's only urban, public research university. The Department is a thriving academic community of scholars, teachers and students who are dedicated to all forms of academic inquiry under the broad umbrella of criminology, law and society, and the study of justice. [4] The members of our faculty, who are well-published scholars in their fields, mentor students to critically examine various justice concerns while adhering to values of diversity, equity, and inclusion. [4] Please Note: The CLJ Department has temporarily paused admission to the MA and PhD programs for administrative reasons—more information to follow. [1, 5]

Requirements:
In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements:

*   Baccalaureate Field: Applicants who intend to specialize in English Studies or English Education must have an undergraduate major in English or the equivalent that includes a balanced program in English and American literature beyond the level of sophomore surveys. Applicants who intend to specialize in Creative Writing may have an undergraduate major or a graduate degree in any field, if they show substantial evidence of ability to complete the work in literature required for the degree in English.
*   Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study and for all graduate work.
*   Tests Required: None, except in cases of English proficiency for some non-native speakers of English.
*   Letters of Recommendation: Three required, preferably from individuals acquainted with the applicant's recent academic, professional, or creative work.
*   Statement of Purpose: Required. Domestic applicants must submit a statement of about 500 words presenting their reasons for wanting to take graduate work in English at UIC and the relationship of this advanced training to professional and other goals. International applicants must submit a two- or three-page summary of their educational experience that emphasizes their work in English and American literature and language.
*   Writing sample: All MA and PhD applicants must submit a sample of their written work. [11]
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Concentration: ['English Studies', 'Creative Writing', 'English Education']
Description: The Graduate Program in English offers a Master of Arts degree in English with three concentrations: one in English Education with and without Illinois teaching licensure, one in English Studies, and one in Creative Writing. [11] A Master's in English from UIC prepares you for a number of careers and vocations within and beyond the academy. [11]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in French and Francophone Studies
Requirements: In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: Baccalaureate Field: A substantial background in French literature is essential, as is fluency in written and spoken French. Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study. Letters of Recommendation: Three required from professors or others familiar with the applicant's recent academic work. Letters are accepted in English or French. [4]
Department: Department of French and Francophone Studies
Concentration: ["Gender and Women's Studies", 'Black Studies']
Description: The Department of French and Francophone Studies offers work leading to the Master of Arts in French and Francophone Studies. UIC's Master of Arts program in French is dynamic and rigorous, blending the benefits of a close-knit academic community with the opportunities of a large urban setting. [3] Classes are small and encourage discussion; students and professors work closely together. Our M.A. program has particular strengths in literary and cultural studies of 17th-, 18th-, 19th-, and 20th-century France, as well as in Francophone literatures of Quebec and Africa. [3] Other faculty interests include film studies, gender studies, religious studies, poetics, and drama. In addition to exploring a broad range of interpretive approaches and cultivating research skills, M.A. students may take advantage of UIC's wonderful Institute for the Humanities, Chicago's famous Art Institute and its vibrant theaters, the vast collections of the Newberry Library, and the MICEFA exchange program in Paris. [3] Graduates of our M.A. program have achieved much success in public- and private-school teaching as well as in a variety of other language-related careers. They also have an excellent record of admission to top PhD programs around the country. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Germanic Studies
Requirements:
Applicants are considered on an individual basis. The program will accept and review applications for fall and spring semesters. Transcripts for all undergraduate and any graduate work must be uploaded along with all other requirements. In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements:

Baccalaureate Field: No restrictions. A substantial background in German literature or culture is expected, as is proficiency in written and spoken German.
Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 in all German courses and in the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study.
Tests Required: None.
Letters of Recommendation (in English): Three required from persons familiar with the applicant's academic work.
Personal Statement: Required; 250 words. The statement should address the applicant's purpose and goals.
Other Requirements: Applicants must submit a sample of their academic writing. Applicants must also take part in an interview (face-to-face or via web conferencing) prior to admittance.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Concentration: ['Black Studies (Interdepartmental Graduate Concentration)', 'Central and Eastern European Studies (Interdepartmental Graduate Concentration)', "Gender and Women's Studies (Interdepartmental Concentration)", 'Jewish Studies']
Description: The Department of Germanic Studies is housed in the heart of Chicago in UIC's School of Literatures, Cultural Studies and Linguistics. Our department is particularly attuned to the linkages between German culture, transnational identities, and urban spaces. [9] UIC is proud to be recognized as of one of the five most ethnically and culturally diverse campuses in the United States and amongst those ranked most highly on the Social Mobility Index. [9] In the Germanic Studies department we actively foster dialogues with the diverse cultural and social groups represented in the university and in the greater Chicago area. [9] The Department of Germanic Studies offers the Master of Arts degree and the Doctor of Philosophy degree in Germanic Studies. [6] Doctoral students may specialize in the fields of Film Studies, Jewish Cultural Studies, Black Studies, Central and Eastern European Studies, Gender and Women's Studies, or Literature and Culture. [6]
ScholarshipType: The program offers opportunities for teaching assistantships, research assistantships, and fellowships. [2, 9]

Requirements: Program-specific requirements (e.g. writing samples, personal statements, resumes, letters of purpose, letters of recommendation, etc.) must be submitted within the application, unless specifically directed to you otherwise by the program to which you are applying. [9]
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description: The MA in History requires 32 semester hours of credit, including two required courses: HIST 501 and a research seminar. The department's fields for the MA are Africa, Asia, Europe (early modern or modern), Latin America, the Middle East, and the United States. Students in the MA program must choose one of these as a major field. The remaining courses are chosen by the student in consultation with his or her advisor. Students may elect to complete a traditional MA thesis or to complete a two-course research-oriented track. All students must also demonstrate a reading knowledge of one foreign language. The MA may be taken as a terminal degree or as a step toward the PhD; for students who do excellent work in the MA program, the department may recommend continuation in the doctoral program.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Latin American and Latino Studies
Requirements:
Applicants are considered on an individual basis. The program will accept and review applications for the fall semester only. Transcripts for all undergraduate and any graduate work must be submitted. In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements:

*   Baccalaureate Field: No restrictions.
*   Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study.
*   Letters of Recommendation: Three letters required, preferably from faculty members in social sciences and humanities. [1]
*   Personal Statement: Required. The statement must address the applicant's professional and academic goals and the candidate's reasons for applying to a Latin American and Latino Studies graduate program. The statement should have a maximum extension of three double-spaced pages. [2]
*   Resume/CV: A resume or CV is required. [1]
Department: Latin American and Latino Studies
Concentration: ['Latin American and Latino Studies (Interdepartmental Concentration)', 'Violence Studies (Interdepartmental Graduate Concentration)']
Description: The mission of the Master of Arts in Latin American and Latino Studies is to offer an interdisciplinary perspective to the study of both contemporary Latin American societies and of Latinos and immigrants of Latin American descent in the United States. This program emphasizes the histories and experiences of Latin American and Latino people as they enter into a transnational dialogue that defines both American and Latin American identities, cultures, economies, and politics in the 21st century. The program encourages an interdisciplinary approach that ranges across the social sciences, humanities, and cultural studies. [8]
Accredidation: The University of Illinois at Chicago is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC) of the North Central Association of Colleges and Schools (NCA). [1, 2]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Museum and Exhibition Studies
Requirements: Applicants are considered on an individual basis. In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: Baccalaureate Field No restrictions. Grade Point Average At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study. The GRE is not required. Three letters of recommendation are required from faculty members or others familiar with the applicant's education, ability, and experience. Applicants must submit a statement of purpose no more than 500 words in length. Applicants must also submit a writing sample of a minimum of 6 pages (1,500 words). Applicants will be contacted to schedule an interview after completing the online application. [3, 4]
Department: School of Art and Art History
Concentration: The Museum and Exhibition Studies (MUSE) Program participates in the Interdepartmental Graduate Concentration in Gender and Women's Studies, which is offered by the Gender and Women's Studies (GWS) program. [3, 5]
Description: The program in Museum and Exhibition Studies (MUSE) in the School of Art and Art History supports study and research leading to the interdisciplinary Master of Arts in Museum and Exhibition Studies. [1, 6] The MA in MUSE offers a synthesis of research and professional practice appropriate to professions in museums and exhibitions. [1, 6] At the University of Illinois at Chicago, the study of Museum and Exhibition Studies places social justice at the core of its work and scholarship. [2] Full-time resident students are required to take five core courses that focus on exhibition-making, collections, writing for exhibitions, public engagement strategies, and the histories of museums and genres. [2] Additionally, students take two capstone research courses, five elective courses, and complete a capstone project or thesis during the two-year program. [2] An optional supervised internship is also available as an elective. [2]
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, assistantships (teaching, research, and graduate), scholarships, tuition waivers

Description: The Department of Philosophy offers work leading to degrees in Philosophy at both the master's and doctoral levels. The MA program requires the completion of 36 semester hours of credit. A minimum of 20 of these hours must be at the 500-level. Of these 20 hours, at least 16 must be in regularly scheduled 500-level philosophy courses. A maximum of 8 hours of PHIL 590 and 16 hours of PHIL 596 are allowed. All 36 hours may be taken in philosophy. With the approval of the department, up to 12 hours may be taken in other departments.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Political Science
Requirements:
In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements:

*   Baccalaureate Field: No restrictions. [7]
*   Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester (90 quarter) hours of undergraduate study. [7]
*   Tests Required: None. [7]
*   Letters of Recommendation: Three are required, preferably from faculty members in political science or cognate disciplines who are familiar with the applicant's training and ability. [7]
*   Personal Statement: Required. The statement should address the applicant's academic goals. [7]
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Concentration: ['American Government and Politics', 'Comparative Politics', 'International Relations', 'Public Policy', 'Security Studies']
Description: The Master of Arts program focuses on the core scholarly Areas of Political Science. Courses in the MA program serve as foundation for work in doctoral program or as preparation for careers in government, nonprofit organizations, or related work in the private sector. [1]

Requirements: In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: Applicants must hold a baccalaureate degree. A GPA of at least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours of undergraduate study is required. Transcripts are required from all institutions where the applicant earned the last 60 semester hours of study. Three letters of recommendation are required, preferably from former or current teachers. The department only accepts applicants who intend to earn the PhD; the MA is earned en route to the doctorate.
Concentration: ["Gender and Women's Studies", 'Latin American and Latino Studies', 'Survey Research Methodology', 'Violence Studies', "Women's Health"]
Description: Students in the Department of Sociology at UIC are prepared to successfully enter academia or research positions in the public sector. The department accepts only applicants to the program who intend to earn the PhD. Students who do not already have an MA in Sociology will earn one as they complete requirements for the doctorate. Course work and research leading to a doctoral degree are concentrated in the area of inequality focusing on the sociology of race, ethnicity, and gender or the sociology of work, organizations, and the economy. Other specialty areas are currently in development.
Accredidation: The University of Illinois Chicago is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [10, 12] Specific accreditation for the Master of Arts in Sociology program is not mentioned.

Requirements: The University of Illinois Chicago (UIC) Business school employs a holistic admission process that evaluates an applicant's undergraduate record, professional experience, personal statement, and letters of recommendation. [12] A 3.0/4.0 undergraduate GPA is preferred. [12, 15] While a business-related undergraduate degree is not a prerequisite, applicants to the MBA program are expected to have at least two years of professional work experience after completing their bachelor's degree. [15] All applicants are required to submit a current CV or resume. [15]
Department: College of Business Administration
Concentration: ['Accounting', 'Business Analytics', 'Economics', 'Entrepreneurship', 'Finance', 'Human Resource Management', 'International Business', 'Management', 'Management Information Systems', 'Marketing', 'Operations and Supply Chain Management', 'Real Estate', 'Self-Directed']
Description: The UIC Business Liautaud Graduate School offers a Master of Business Administration with concentrations in Accounting, Business Analytics, Economics, Entrepreneurship, Finance, Human Resource Management, International Business, Management, Management Information Systems, Marketing, Operations and Supply Chain Management, Real Estate, and a Self-Directed option. [3] Students may complete the program by selecting among four different enrollment options: Flexible (full-time or part-time enrollment), Accelerated, or Online. [3] Students may start the on-campus Flexible full- or part-time program in the fall, spring, or summer semester. [3]
Accredidation: The UIC Business Liautaud Graduate School is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International). [7]

Requirements:
Applicants are considered on an individual basis. In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program admission criteria:

Baccalaureate Field: Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Urban Studies, Urban Planning, and other creative fields. Relevant professional experience of two or more years is strongly recommended.
Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study. [2, 3]
Tests Required: None required for admission. [2, 3]
Letters of Recommendation: Three required. [2, 3]
Personal Statement: Required. The statement must address the applicant’s educational and career goals and previous pertinent work, volunteer, and/or academic experience. [2, 3]
Other Requirements: Applicants must submit a portfolio comprising their most important and representative visual arts, design, research, and/or professional work such as an essay, academic paper or policy report, newspaper article, photographs, handmade sketches, computer-generated graphics, design proposal, or project of which they are the sole author or designer. [2, 3] Applicants must submit a resume as well. [2, 3]
Description: The Master of City Design (MCD) is a 10-month intensive graduate degree focusing on the built environment and addressing pressing racial, spatial, and climatic inequality issues. [2] Hands-on field-based studio learning provides immersive exposure to integrated, interdisciplinary design approaches and professional practice in urban places across Chicago. [2] Our diverse and interdisciplinary curriculum integrates urban design with climate science, community economic development, environmental planning, public policy, and transportation equity. [2]
Accredidation: No specialized accreditation, licensure nor certification requirements exist for the proposed Master of City Design. [11]

Requirements: In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements for the School of Design. Baccalaureate Field: No restrictions; however, individuals who apply must demonstrate an advanced level of competence in graphic design through their portfolio submission. Grade Point Average: At least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study. [10]
Department: College of Architecture, Design, and the Arts
Concentration: ['Graphic Design', 'Industrial Design']
Description: The Master of Design (MDes) in Graphic Design or Industrial Design prepares designers to make substantive contributions that advance the profession and improve our world. [2] Focused on independent research projects, students explore a topic of inquiry with the potential to inform and shape disciplinary knowledge. [2] Applicants from any background are welcome in the MDes program. [2] Students applying directly to the two-year program are expected to demonstrate a record of professional experience in design and to present a considerable and significant portfolio of work. [2] Applicants who do not hold a bachelor's degree in design may be eligible for one year of prerequisite coursework, customized per student, in preparation for the two-year MDes sequence. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Illinois Chicago is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [10, 11] Information regarding specific accreditation for the Master of Design program by an accrediting body such as the National Association of Schools of Art and Design is not available on the university's website.

Requirements: Applicants must meet the admission criteria of the Graduate College, including a minimum grade point average of 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study.
Concentration: ['MEd Early Childhood Education', 'MEd Instructional Leadership - Educational Studies', 'MEd Instructional Leadership - Policy Studies', 'MEd Language, Literacies & Learning', 'MEd Measurement, Evaluation, Statistics & Assessment (MESA) on-campus', 'MEd Measurement, Evaluation, Statistics & Assessment (MESA) Online', 'MEd Science Education', 'MEd Special Education', 'MEd Urban Higher Education', 'MEd Youth Development']
Description: Our Master of Education (MEd) programs are for people who are or want to become teachers, researchers, and educational leaders. Our master's students work with our faculty, graduate students, and community partners to develop research and practical experience in Chicago's schools and community-based organizations. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Illinois Chicago is institutionally accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). [22, 23] The curricula for teacher preparation have been approved by the Illinois Board of Higher Education and the Illinois State Board of Education (ISBE). [22] The Council on Teacher Education (CTE) at UIC oversees all teacher preparation programs, including licensure and endorsements. [21]

ProgramName: Master of Education in Early Childhood Education
Requirements: Applicants must complete the UIC Graduate Admissions application. Required documents include undergraduate transcripts for the last 60 hours of the undergraduate degree and all graduate transcripts. For international applicants, TOEFL or IELTS test scores are necessary. Three letters of recommendation are required, which should address academic qualifications, research ability/experience, and the capacity for advanced degree studies. At least one letter should be from someone who can speak to the applicant's experience with children. Additionally, applicants must complete a questionnaire and a written statement regarding their experience with young children. [5]
Department: College of Education
Description: The MEd in Early Childhood Education is a blended early childhood and early childhood special education program designed to prepare program completers to work with all children and their families. [2] The primary focus is on preparing teachers, but program completers also are qualified for other roles including working as a developmental therapists and leadership roles in early childhood settings. [2] UIC's master's program in Early Childhood Education reflects the most recent scholarly advances about the cultural and contextual nature of children's learning, while also responding to the needs of the Chicagoland community. [2] The program was the first in the state of Illinois to prepare teachers to work with all young children regardless of ability, and is today still one of very few that offer blended curriculum in early childhood and early childhood special education. [2] The program educates professionals dedicated to working with young children and their families across a wide range of settings. [2]
Accredidation: During the program, students have the opportunity to earn an Illinois Professional Educator License (PEL) with an endorsement in Early Childhood Education and Early Childhood Special Education, the Illinois Gateways Level 5 Early Childhood Education credential, and/or the Illinois Early Intervention credential. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Education in Instructional Leadership
Requirements: In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: Baccalaureate Field No restrictions. Grade Point Average: Recommended minimum of 2.75/4.00 for the final 60 semester (90 quarter) hours of undergraduate study and at least 3.00/4.00 for all postbaccalaureate/graduate coursework. [2]
Department: College of Education
Concentration: ['Educational Studies', 'Policy Studies']
Description: The Policy Studies a concentration within the Instructional Leadership MEd program allows students to design their own programs of study toward deepening understandings of how to support underserved communities in Chicago and beyond. [6] The MEd in Instructional Leadership - Policy Studies provides students with knowledge and resources to support historically marginalized populations gain access to increased educational opportunities. [6] Housed within the Educational Policy Studies Department, this master's degree offers students the flexibility to select a strand of study related to their personal and professional goals. [6] The Educational Studies concentration within the MEd Instructional Leadership program enables students to design their own course of study with guidance from an adviser. Individuals from a variety of backgrounds (art, sports, business, humanities, higher education, etc.) can pursue a course of study tailored to their backgrounds, interests, and personal & professional aspirations. Also, if an applicant currently holds a professional teacher licensure s/he can earn endorsements to their PEL and /or pursue advanced studies in educational topics (although having a teacher license is not required for this program).

ProgramName: Master of Education in Language, Literacies, and Learning
Requirements: In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: a recommended minimum GPA of 2.75/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours of undergraduate study and at least 3.00 for all postbaccalaureate/graduate coursework, two letters of recommendation, a resume, and a personal statement (500–1000 words). [2] For certain endorsements, an Illinois Professional Educator License (PEL) is required, and the Reading Specialist endorsement requires a minimum of two years of teaching experience. [1, 2]
Department: College of Education
Description: The MEd in Language, Literacies, and Learning provides advanced training for educators and other professionals who work with linguistically and culturally diverse learners in urban settings. This program prepares individuals for a variety of roles, such as bilingual and English as a Second Language (ESL) teachers, literacy or reading specialists, and language and literacy leaders in schools and communities. The curriculum is designed to help students develop a deep understanding of the sociopolitical and sociocultural contexts of language and literacy education, as well as the theoretical and practical knowledge needed to design and implement effective and equitable instruction and assessment. Students in this program will engage in coursework that focuses on first and second language acquisition, bilingualism and biliteracy, multicultural literatures, digital and media literacies, and disciplinary literacies. They will also have opportunities to participate in supervised clinical experiences in schools and community-based organizations. Through this combination of coursework and fieldwork, graduates will be prepared to become leaders and advocates for educational equity and social justice.
MinGPA: 2.75/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours of undergraduate study and 3.00 for all postbaccalaureate/graduate coursework

ProgramName: Master of Education in Measurement, Evaluation, Statistics, and Assessment
Requirements:
In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements:

*   Baccalaureate Field: No restrictions.
*   Grade Point Average: At least 2.75/4.00 for the final 60 semester (90 quarter) hours of undergraduate study, and a 3.00/4.00 on all postbaccalaureate or graduate course work combined. [2]
*   Tests Required: GRE General optional but preferred. Students not submitting the GRE General should submit other evidence to support their application showing their readiness for the MEd in MESA. Description: The online Master of Education in Measurement, Evaluation, Statistics and Assessment (MESA) degree provides you with a blend of theoretical knowledge and hands-on application of new skills. The program teaches you to determine the best method to collect data, how to consider multiple avenues to analyze data, and how to interpret and effectively communicate the data. [1] The curriculum is designed for students interested in research positions in a variety of settings including;. school districts,; academic institutions,; federal, state and local agencies; public and private testing organizations including licensure and certification boards and; medical and health care organizations. The curriculum is also well suited for students pursuing a PhD in education or other research-intensive fields. [1]

Strand A (Licensure option) requires a GPA of 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours of undergraduate study, a 3.00 for any postbaccalaureate/graduate coursework, and a 2.50/4.00 in a science field. Description: The Master's in Education Program (MEd) in Science Education offers graduate study for educators in the sciences across a range of institutional, community, career, and disciplinary contexts. [10] There are two options: Strand A includes entitlement to an Illinois Professional Educators (PEL) license with high school or middle grades science endorsements; Strand B has an emphasis on out-of-school science education contexts, or an advanced-studies focus for experienced teachers or educators interested in exploring career trajectories in research. [10] The program is aligned with the mission, vision, and values of the UIC College of Education, preparing science educators who transform education to advance justice and liberation. [10] It envisions science education that fosters human flourishing and values engagement, hope, and justice in and through science learning contexts within and beyond schools. [10]
Accredidation: The Illinois State Board of Education (ISBE) approves the program for licensure. [11] The UIC catalog notes that the ISBE is not an accreditation agency but approves programs for licensure. [11]

Description: The MEd in Special Education prepares graduates to work with people with disabilities, diverse in strengths, ages (5-21), and teaching and learning in educational and community settings, and schools. [3] The need for special education teachers is urgent, especially in urban areas like Chicago. [3] Research indicates that a shortage of special education teachers disproportionately affects minority students, particularly in urban school districts that have large majorities of African American and Latina/o/x students. [3] Special educators work in a range of instructional settings in school and in communities. [3] All students earn a master's and can add on initial Illinois licensure and credentials. [3] The program welcomes students entirely new to teaching, current teachers new to special education, current special education teachers and students seeking new knowledge about special education. [3]

Description: The MEd in Urban Higher Education program develops equity-oriented and principled leaders in higher education who understand the urban context, foster racial justice, promote equity and diversity, and use research and theory to help higher education institutions and individuals within them thrive. [1] The experiences, knowledge and skills gained from this program can prepare graduates for the competitive pursuit of positions in public or private institutions. Graduates could find opportunities in entry level and mid-level college and/or university leadership positions. [1] Potential areas of professional opportunity include residence life and campus housing, student activities, Greek affairs, recreation center/sports, academic advising, admissions, financial aid, and administrative support. In addition, the transferable knowledge and skills of this program could help graduates pursue opportunities outside of a college or university setting. Another option and benefit of the program is preparation for a doctoral program. [1]

Description: The MEd in Youth Development program will prepare you to create and impact spaces, programs, and organizations in urban contexts to support youth in developing their social, emotional, physical, and intellectual selves. Program courses and curriculum are designed to develop youth-dedicated professionals who understand the diverse contexts where youth learn and live. Graduates understand and value engagement with community and school stakeholders to foster youth's strengths. The Youth Development program focuses on: Youth as agents of change; Urban environments; Positive psychology/strengths; Context and culture; Social justice; Self-reflection. [11]

Description: The demand for energy engineers continues unabated. This master’s program covers the waterfront of the energy industry, from energy-efficient buildings to power production and storage. Whether your interest is in HVAC design, energy efficiency, management of engineering projects, or power from production to storage to delivery, you will graduate with knowledge that can be immediately applied on the job. A Master of Energy Engineering degree will expand your career opportunities by increasing your knowledge of energy engineering.

[7] A cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the final 60 semester hours of undergraduate study is required. [7] For those without an engineering or computer science major, specific calculus and science courses are mandated. [7] International applicants must hold a 4-year Bachelor's degree or its equivalent. [7] While not a strict requirement, the admissions committee considers individuals whose professional engineering experience is a distinguishing factor, even if academic requirements are not fully met. Description: The Master of Engineering (MEng) is a professional master's degree intended to provide a student with subject matter expertise that can be directly applied to a career in industry, government, or consulting. [6] It is primarily a course-only master's degree, although a project course is an option. [6] It is not a research-oriented degree and does not require a thesis. [6] The curriculum is based on courses only, which allows for degree completion in one year. [9] The MEng degree is available on campus and online. [6] The degree requires 32 semester hours of credit, with a minimum of 20 hours at the 500-level. [6]
Accredidation: Master's and PhD programs are not accredited by ABET. [15] The University of Illinois Chicago is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [10]

Description: The Master of Fine Arts in Art is a professional degree for artists who wish to teach at the college level and for those who wish to pursue a career as a practicing artist. The School of Art and Art History graduate program is interdisciplinary. Graduate students are not admitted to a specific media area and are free to work in any and all media. The school provides a foundation in critical theory and art history, as well as a rigorous studio practice to prepare students to enter the professional art world. The program is committed to a curriculum that is exploratory and that supports a wide range of artistic production, from traditional media to emerging technologies and social engagement. The curriculum for the MFA degree is designed to be flexible to accommodate the diverse needs of our students. All students work closely with our internationally recognized faculty in graduate seminars and through one-on-one advising and critiques. Students are also encouraged to work with faculty from other departments and to take advantage of the many resources available at a major research university. The School of Art and Art History views the city of Chicago as an extension of the classroom and encourages students to engage with the city’s rich cultural landscape.

Requirements: Applicants must hold a baccalaureate degree or an advanced professional degree in a health professions discipline. Applicants with a degree in a related field and significant experience in a health professions setting will also be considered. A GPA of at least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours (90 quarter hours) of undergraduate study is required. [2] Applicant must submit a written statement of their professional goals (personal statement), a CV, and three letters of recommendation. [1]

Description: The Master of Health Professions Education (MHPE) program at the University of Illinois Chicago is designed for individuals with a deep interest in Health Professions Education (HPE) who desire additional leadership and scholarship skills to advance their education, research, and career. [6] Situated in one of the first and largest medical education departments in the world, the program is globally recognized as a leader in HPE. [6] The purpose of the MHPE program is to provide the education necessary to produce effective leaders and scholars in health professions education. [7] Students acquire the knowledge and skills needed to become leaders and scholars in HPE, developing proficiency in key education concepts and theories, including curriculum design and implementation, instruction and learning, assessment of performance, and program evaluation. [6] They also develop proficiency in HPE leadership, including organizational analysis and the use of tools for assessing, leading, and managing individual and organizational change in the HPE context. [6] Disciplinary and interdisciplinary offerings are available on topics related to management and leadership in health professions education, scholarship methods, curriculum, instruction, competence assessment, program evaluation, and medical humanities and ethics. [7] The program is designed for professionals working full-time and is typically completed on a part-time basis within 3 years. [6]

Prior experience in healthcare is not required; however, the MHA program does give consideration to applicants with relevant professional work experience, superior credentials, and demonstrated leadership potential. Description: The master of public health concentration in health policy and administration (HPA) programs partner with students to develop and advance their careers in public health through coursework in health policy development and management while learning the basic principles of public health. Inter-professional faculty with expertise in public policy, health economics, law, management, disparities research, global information systems, and public health informatics teach our courses.
Accredidation: The University of Illinois at Chicago School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: Master of Physiology for Therapeutic Development
Department: College of Medicine

Description: The Master of Physiology for Therapeutic Development (MaPTD) is a newly developed one-year, classroom-based program in Chicago designed to prepare students for impactful careers in clinical trial research, implementation, and enrollment. [1] As clinical trials become increasingly complex and diverse, the demand for professionals who fully understand the scientific, regulatory, and operational aspects of trials has grown. This program addresses that need by offering comprehensive training in all facets of clinical trials—from trial design and regulatory affairs to participant recruitment and data interpretation. [3] At its foundation, the MaPTD provides rigorous education in human physiology and disease, enabling students to translate scientific discoveries into rational, patient-centered trial designs. With this integrated approach, graduates will be uniquely equipped to support and improve clinical trial execution in both academic and biopharmaceutical settings, ultimately enhancing trial enrollment and the development of effective therapies. [3] The MaPTD is a one-year program that provides students with advanced training in human physiological sciences and enhanced preparation for professional careers in the health sciences, particularly in the biopharmaceutical industry. By providing a program based in human physiology—one of the most important basic areas of the health sciences—the curriculum will not only provide graduate-level education, but will also help students attain lucrative positions in the broad biopharmaceutical industry. [2]

[6] The program's faculty have academic training and research interests covering a broad range of relevant areas including law, management, political science, statistics and research methods, survey research, sociology, economics, business, organizational theory and decision making, human resources, budgeting and finance, and information technology. [15]
Accredidation: The MPA is a professional program fully accredited by the National Association of Schools of Public Affairs and Administration. [6, 10]

Description: The Master of Public Policy (MPP) is a professional degree program designed to develop leaders who can put evidence-first. In course work, students build critical thinking and analytical skills in the core curriculum and learn to make data-driven decisions. Through applied experiences in Chicago and beyond, they will meet face-to-face with professionals in the field to analyze urgent policy problems and design solutions that work, using the latest science and technology. The core curriculum draws on a variety of disciplines and fields, including economics, sociology, political science, statistics, econometrics, political economy, organizational theory, and program evaluation. This is an ideal fit for students seeking a multidisciplinary approach to the study of public policy.

Whether you picture yourself as a CPA, Controller, Managerial Accountant or a different career in business, UIC Business's Master of Science in Accounting degree helps you get there. As of January 2025, the MS in Accounting is a STEM-designated degree. [13] The Accounting program prepares leaders to develop the professional skills identified by the Institute of Certified Public Accountants deemed essential for providing the core accounting services across various fields, including corporate accounting, assurance services, taxation, internal audit, government/nonprofit, and ERP/SAP systems. [1] Upon completion of the program, students may be eligible to sit for the Uniform CPA Exam, provided they meet the requirements of each state's board of public accountancy. [1]

Courses are specifically designed to meet the needs of elementary and middle school teachers. Students in this master's program are typically full-time elementary and middle school teachers. Courses are offered in the late afternoon and early evening. Some courses are also offered during the summer. Students complete a final practicum designed to improve the mathematics education in their home school.

It aims to develop students' written and oral communication skills, refine their research and analytical abilities for better decision-making, and instill a commitment to lifelong learning. The program prepares leaders with the professional skills identified by the Institute of Certified Public Accountants, which are essential for core accounting services in fields like corporate accounting, assurance services, taxation, internal audit, government/nonprofit, and ERP/SAP systems. Graduates may be eligible to sit for the Uniform CPA Exam, depending on state board requirements. The program has two options: MS Accounting Flex, which allows students to customize their degree with tracks in professional accounting, tax, internal audit, accounting analytics, and research, with courses available in various formats; and MS Accounting Cohort, a two-year program where students learn together and can opt for a second Master of Science degree in Business Analytics. Description: The Master of Science in Biomedical Engineering is designed to prepare students for careers in industry, business, academia, and research lab environments by offering a flexible program of coursework and mentoring that enables them to engage in creative and independent research on a cutting-edge topic. [2] The program is strongly interdisciplinary, with areas of study including Cell and Tissue Engineering, Diagnostics, Neural Engineering and Rehabilitation, Bioinformatics and Genomics, Medical Imaging, Bio- and Cellular Mechanics, Biomaterials, and Nanobiomolecular Engineering. [15] Students can choose between a thesis track, which is ideal for those considering a PhD, and a non-thesis track. [10] The thesis track involves research with a faculty advisor and results in a paper suitable for conference presentation or journal submission. [3] The non-thesis track consists entirely of coursework. [3] A master's degree in biomedical engineering from UIC prepares students for a variety of careers, including as researchers in academic, industry, or government laboratories; researchers in medical schools and hospitals; and in research and development positions at companies. Such students may be required to take a specified sequence of undergraduate chemical engineering courses to make up for deficiencies. Letters of Recommendation: Not required for MS applicants; required for PhD applicants. Personal Statement: Required. A one-to-three page statement of the applicant’s professional goals and reasons for wishing to pursue graduate study in chemical engineering at UIC.
Description: The Master's of Science program in Chemical Engineering is intended for students who wish to pursue advanced studies and research in chemical engineering. A thesis is required for the degree. The program is designed to provide excellent preparation for a career in research and development in industry or academia. The program is specifically designed to achieve a number of objectives and to provide students with a set of learning outcomes. Program Objectives To graduate master-level chemical engineers who are highly qualified for rewarding professional experiences. To provide graduates with a high level of competence in fundamental and applied concepts of chemical engineering. To provide graduates with an environment in which they can embrace social and personal development. To motivate graduates to seek life-long learning and professional development. To enhance graduates' recognition and understanding of their professional and societal responsibilities. To help graduates develop their computational techniques and written and oral communication skills. To cultivate innovation and entrepreneurship through deeper understanding and advanced knowledge of chemical engineering principles and operations. Program Learning Outcomes Upon graduation, students will be able to: Apply advanced concepts of fundamental sciences and engineering to solve complex chemical engineering problems. Demonstrate the ability to work effectively both independently and in teams of various backgrounds. Apply innovative and practical solutions to existing or novel processes in research. Search, evaluate, and acquire information from relevant chemical engineering literature. Design advanced approaches to conduct chemical engineering experiments. Use advanced quantitative and qualitative methods to interpret research experimental results. Disseminate and discuss their professional and scientific work with the general public as well as with experts in both written and oral formats. Observe and apply ethical and professional codes and responsibilities.

Through the careful selection of courses, you can tailor the UIC MS in Civil Engineering program to meet your interests and needs. This option is available for part-time as well as full-time students. [2]

Description: The 100% online asynchronous Master of Science in Health Information Management (MSHIM) program curriculum encompasses medical records, use and storage of patient data, coding, and leadership. [1] Learn how to manage healthcare data and information resources. [1] Acquire the expertise necessary to take and pass the prestigious Registered Health Information Administrator (RHIA) certification exam. [1] Examine the social, ethical, organizational, and legal issues associated with health information systems and electronic health records. [1] Explore a detailed analysis of various health information systems and study the pressing legal, security and privacy issues associated with the management of electronic medical records. [1] The 39-credit hour program is housed within University of Illinois Chicago (UIC) College of Applied Health Sciences and can be completed in 20 months. [1] The Master of Science in Health Information Management degree is designed to impart the knowledge and critical skills important for helping organizations develop and implement effective health information management strategies, advance the quality of patient care and safeguard the integrity of electronic health records. [1] Many areas of study are covered in this 100% online program to help prepare students for the various roles defined by health information management. [1]
Accredidation: The Health Information Management accreditor of University of Illinois Chicago is the Commission on Accreditation for Health Informatics and Information Management Education (CAHIIM). The College's accreditation for Master of Science degree in Health Information Management has been reaffirmed through 2030. [1]

The Master of Science in Industrial Engineering (MSIE) degree program provides a graduate-level introduction to the broad field of industrial engineering. [1] The program consists of graduate-level coursework in operations research, statistics, and applied industrial engineering. [1] Students in the program study under faculty actively engaged in research and prepared to teach the latest developments in industrial engineering. [1] Students interested in a follow-on doctor al a study should find that the program provides an excellent introduction to graduate study and outstanding preparation for in-depth study. [1] The MSIE program consists of 30 credit hours with core courses in manufacturing, warehousing, and supply chain systems, as well as methodology courses such as simulation, optimization, and probabilistic models. Description: The Master of Science in Medical Biotechnology will train students in the major techniques and disciplines commonly used in biotechnology. Course subjects may include recombinant DNA and molecular biology techniques, immunotechnology, protein chemistry and proteomics, drug design and drug development processes, medical implants, stem cell therapy, and nanotechnology. In addition, students will receive direct experience with many of the analytical and testing techniques used in the biotechnology and healthcare industries. Workplace-related training will include an introduction to pertinent regulatory issues and practices, basic training in grant proposal preparation and public presentation of a technical topic, and training in program management systems and product development processes.

[1] With a large and diverse faculty and student body, the MUPP program offers a comprehensive range of courses, including many specialized electives and studios. Graduates can connect to a large network of alumni, both locally and across the region, country, and world. [1]

Description: The Master of Design (MDes) in Industrial Design is a two-year degree program focused on an independent master's research project that offers students the opportunity to identify and explore a topic of inquiry with the potential to contribute to broader disciplinary knowledge. [10] The program's mission is to create dynamic thinkers/makers who view design holistically in terms of objects, systems and services and can simultaneously bridge the gap between each speculative outcome and its broader context. [10] In this era, Industrial Design transcends the notion of object; an object is no longer a singular embodiment, but an essential part of a larger, complex system of meaning. [5] Every aspect of design now influences a larger ecosystem impacting the economy, environment, technology, manufacturing, and society as a whole. [5] Designers work today within cross-functional teams solving complex issues and UIC Design education reflects this new reality. [5] Advanced technologies are integrated into the curriculum as tools to enable and facilitate outcomes. [5] The substantive advancement in design education is in the process of creating designers who think dynamically and holistically in terms of objects, systems and services and can simultaneously bridge the gap between each speculative outcome and its broader context. [5] Extensive multidisciplinary research is brought into the classroom by way of coursework, sponsored research, lectures, and critiques, challenging students to understand how their design may be viewed and understood through a range of lenses. [5] The UIC School of Design continues to be a leader in strengthening the synthesis of thinking and making across objects and communications serving as the catalyst for innovative development and the future of design practice. The program culminates in a public exhibition of the master's research project. [5]

Department: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) is a degree type offered by numerous colleges within the university, including but not limited to the College of Applied Health Sciences, College of Architecture, Design, and the Arts, College of Business Administration, College of Education, College of Engineering, and College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, all under the administrative oversight of the Graduate College.
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) is a doctoral degree offered across numerous fields of study at the University of Illinois Chicago. General university requirements for doctoral degrees stipulate that a minimum of 96 semester hours from the baccalaureate or at least 64 from the master's degree are required; however, some degree programs may require more. [4] Candidates who hold a prior master's degree may be granted 32 semester hours of credit toward their doctoral degree. [4] At least 48 semester hours beyond the master's level must be taken at UIC, and only 400- and 500-level courses can be applied to the degree. [4] Students admitted with a master's degree must complete their doctoral degree requirements within seven consecutive years, while those proceeding directly from a bachelor's degree must complete the requirements within nine years. [4] The PhD program develops scholars capable of conducting original research and teaching in their respective fields. [9] While specific curricula are designed by the individual programs to meet the interests and goals of the student, all PhD programs culminate in a dissertation that represents an original contribution to the field. [9, 4]
MaxFails: The university does not specify a maximum number of failing grades. Instead, graduate students are required to maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00. Failure to maintain this GPA or make satisfactory progress can result in an 'academic warning' and subsequent dismissal ('dropped' status) if the requirements are not met within a specified timeframe. [1]
ScholarshipType: The official university catalog implies the availability of 'assistantships' and 'fellowships' as forms of financial support for graduate students. [1]

In addition to the Graduate College minimum requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements: a Master's Degree is required, a Grade Point Average of at least 3.00/4.00 for the final 60 semester hours of undergraduate study and for all postbaccalaureate coursework, and three letters of recommendation are required. Description: The EdD in Urban Education Leadership is a nationally-recognized program designed to prepare and develop principals who are able to lead the improvement of teaching and learning in urban schools. The program faculty and staff are comprised of equity-minded educators committed to developing aspiring leaders who have the drive to disrupt inequities and advance learning opportunities within diverse student populations. This an intensive, highly-selective cohort program combining coursework with supervised practicum experiences at the school level. It leads to the Illinois Principal Endorsement after successful completion of the first 18 months of coursework and residency, and to the Ed.D. degree upon three more years of successful leadership and study. [3]

Department: College of Applied Health Sciences
Description: The Doctor of Clinical Exercise Physiology (DCEP) program at UIC provides unique didactic and practical training opportunities that elevate the professional preparation beyond what is currently available for students who aspire to practice as clinical exercise physiologists. [1] The program builds upon a master's degree training and delivers rigorous didactic and practical education that includes the clinical management of patients with complex health conditions, performing echocardiograms, delivering diabetes education to patients and effectively managing clinical programs and personnel. [1] The DCEP is the advanced degree for individuals who wish to become clinical exercise physiologists. At the University of Illinois Chicago, students complete three terms (12 months) of didactic and clinical education that includes lecture and laboratory courses, seminars, and clinical internships. [2] The program offers unique opportunities to work with different patient populations including those with cardiovascular disease, pulmonary conditions, pediatric cardiopulmonary conditions, chronic kidney disease, metabolic disorders, and cancer; access to the University of Illinois Medical Center, including opportunities for clinical observations; opportunities to expand their skillset with cardiovascular imaging and providing diabetes education to patients; and world-class faculty specializing in chronic diseases, including researchers with labs on site. [2]
ScholarshipType: The College of Applied Health Sciences offers several scholarships for which students can apply, such as need-based and merit-based awards. [9, 11, 15] Students can use the UIC Scholarship and Awards Program (SnAP) system to find and apply for various opportunities. [11]

Description: The UIC College of Dentistry offers an innovative pre-doctoral degree program, the Doctor of Dental Medicine (DMD). The program is designed to graduate oral health professionals with strong competencies in health promotion and disease prevention, diagnosis, evidence-based practice, communication, collaboration, and community engagement. This is a full time, year-round four-year program with a fall term start. The program spans four years and includes an extramural clinical experience in the fourth year.

These include two courses of general biology with laboratory, two courses of general chemistry with laboratory, two courses of organic chemistry with laboratory, one course of biochemistry, two courses of general physics with laboratory, one course of advanced-level biology, and three courses in the Behavioral/Social Sciences. All candidates must take the Medical College Admissions Test (MCAT). A minimum of three academic or professional letters of recommendation are also required. [4, 8]

Description: The University of Illinois Chicago (UIC) Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) degree is designed for professional nurses seeking a terminal degree in nursing with a focus on clinical or administrative practice. [2, 9] The DNP program is consistent with the American Association of Colleges of Nursing's call to produce advanced nursing clinicians who are able to address complex care needs. [9] In addition, it is supported by the National Academy of Science which has advocated for the development of professional practice doctorates as a route to advanced clinical work in nursing. [9] The DNP degree curriculum at UIC consists of three domains of competencies for advanced practice in direct clinical care or systems: a) core practice competencies, b) specialty-specific practice competencies, and c) role competencies. [9] Our mission is to develop advanced practitioners of nursing into evidence-based, intra-disciplinary providers who meet the needs of a rapidly expanding healthcare field. [9]
Accredidation: The DNP is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE). [2, 9]

Description: UIC's entry-level occupational therapy doctoral degree program is designed for students who have a bachelor's or master's degree in another subject and want to become occupational therapists. [3] Our curriculum prepares you for the national certification exam and practice as an OT. [3] The program's two-year, nine-month, full-time curriculum features innovative teaching strategies that emphasize embedded, real-life learning, such as problem-based learning, flipped classroom, and simulation with standardized patients. [3] Students learn to integrate occupational therapy practice, theory and research, gain skills to engage in ethical and high-quality practice, and are prepared to become leaders and advocates in a wide variety of settings. [3] The curriculum includes 28 didactic or seminar classroom-based courses covering theory, evidence-based clinical practice skills, leadership, management, program development, and foundations for capstone work. [3, 5]
Accredidation: UIC's entry-level Doctor of Occupational Therapy (E-OTD) program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) of the American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA). [5, 8]

Admission criteria include demonstrated academic ability, good moral character, proficiency and clarity in both written and spoken English, strong potential for professional outlook and behavior, evidence of leadership and maturity, and complete mental and physical competence to perform all tasks regularly expected of a registered pharmacist. [5] Applicants must complete a PharmCAS application and, if invited, a UIC Supplemental Application. [5] To be considered, applicants must complete a minimum of 18 required pre-pharmacy courses with a C- grade or better and have cumulative, required pre-pharmacy coursework, and combined science/math coursework grade point averages of 2.50/4.00 or better. [5]

The concentrations utilize the expertise and areas of study from all three departments within the college: Pharmaceutical Sciences; Pharmacy Systems, Outcomes and Policy; and Pharmacy Practice.

Description: Physical therapists are experts in how the body moves. When injury, disease or disability interferes nodules life with work, physical therapists help their clients to correct (or prevent the progression of) movement disorders. They help people stay healthy and fit, and prevent the onset or progression of impairments brought on by injury, disease, disorders and disabilities. A Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) is the entry-level degree for people who want to become physical therapists. At UIC, you'll complete eight terms (33 months) of didactic and clinical education that includes lecture courses, laboratory courses, seminars, and clinical internships, preparing you for a career as a physical therapist. Our students have access to the University of Illinois Hospital (UI Health) and a world-class faculty in all major physical therapy specialties, including researchers with labs on campus. Additionally, you can develop your clinical interests further by pursuing electives and courses in areas such as gait, pediatrics, gender health, and sports physical therapy. You will be well-prepared for your career in physical therapy.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) program at the University of Illinois at Chicago is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE), 3030 Potomac Ave., Suite 100, Alexandria, Virginia 22305-3085; telephone: 703-706-3245; email: accreditation@apta.org; website: capteonline.org. Physical therapist education at UIC has been continuously accredited by CAPTE since 1973. The DPT program is the only program accredited by CAPTE that is offered by the Department of Physical Therapy. CAPTE conducted a review of the program in 2017, at which time the program received full (10 year) accreditation until 2027.

Description: The Doctor of Public Health (DrPH) is the advanced professional degree offered by the School of Public Health. This program is tailored to meet the goals of mid-career public health professionals who want to expand their knowledge and practice of public health and attain the leadership skills necessary to enable them to advance the field. The program aims to help students become leaders of the public health community at the local, national, and international levels. The curriculum integrates and assures achievement of learning aligned with the Council on Education in Public Health (CEPH) and UIC DrPH program competencies grounded in equity and transformational leadership. The program is offered in a synchronous, distance-based model.

Description: The Department of Anthropology at the University of Illinois Chicago offers a PhD program designed for candidates with a strong theoretical foundation and research base, who can also translate this knowledge to the classroom. [8] The program emphasizes training students with solid theoretical and methodological skills to enhance their research and career goals. [7] All students, regardless of whether they enter with a bachelor's or master's degree, must complete five core courses in their first year, which provide a foundational knowledge of cultural theory, archaeology, biological anthropology, and career development. [8, 7] The department has research laboratories for studies in archaeology, sociocultural anthropology, and biological anthropology. [12] A key feature of the program is its collaborative PhD program with the Field Museum, which allows curators from the museum to mentor and train graduate students. This collaboration provides students with access to the museum's laboratories, collections, and other facilities, and is particularly utilized by archaeology students. [12] Students can also pursue interdepartmental concentrations. [6, 12]

[2] Doctoral students work alongside faculty mentors to conduct investigations in their labs, and they also may have the opportunity to develop classroom skills as teaching assistants. [2] Our doctoral programs produce top-tier candidates for high-level industry jobs, postdoctoral research positions, and tenure-track faculty roles at universities around the world. The PhD in Civil Engineering degree is awarded to candidates who successfully complete a program of advanced courses and research and defend a dissertation. Students are expected to conduct an independent investigation in a civil engineering research area under the direction of a faculty advisor. The objective of the program is to produce graduates who are able to meet the challenges of the civil engineering discipline and to provide innovative solutions based on the most recent developments in civil engineering.

Description: The PhD program in Communication at the University of Illinois at Chicago trains students to generate new knowledge about communication. [11] The program has a specific focus on technology as a key factor that has transformed the discipline, particularly the rise of interactive digital communication. [11] The department's curriculum is based on modes of inquiry rather than narrowly focused job skills, helping students learn how to learn. [11] Through the study of communication theory, criticism, and methods, students learn to research, analyze, and articulate solutions to communication problems across various media and settings. [11] The department's mission is to enhance critical awareness of self and others within a wide range of communication contexts, from personal to public, emphasizing how communication establishes, sustains, and transforms interpersonal, institutional, and intercultural life. [11]

ProgramName: PhD in Criminology, Law, and Justice

Students with an MA from another institution must satisfy UIC Criminology, Law, and Justice MA requirements. [1]
